title: PP Registry Wiring — Connect 910 Machines, 2,957 Materials, 95K Tools to Pipeline
description: Wire MachineRegistry, MaterialRegistry, and ToolRegistry into PostProcessorPipelineEngine._resolveContexts(). Replace hardcoded defaults (max_rpm=12000, 4-flute carbide, regex ISO group) with catalog lookups. Route Stage 1.1 through SpeedFeedOrchestratorEngine instead of direct UltimateSpeedFeedEngine call. Wire user-proven-cutting-data.ts as validation anchor. This is the highest-ROI change: it activates ALL existing physics with REAL data.

engines: PostProcessorPipelineEngine (3,149 lines) — the pipeline being wired
SpeedFeedOrchestratorEngine (2,851 lines) — 8 resolvers, MC UQ, currently bypassed
UltimateSpeedFeedEngine (3,005 lines) — current direct call target
formulas: Kienzle kc1.1 (already in constants.ts — must import, not inline)
tribal: TribalKnowledgeEngine (3,700+ tips) — Stage 5.3 currently hardcoded, defer to MS2

forge_triple.protective_hook: pp-registry-check — blocks PP engine edits that add hardcoded material/machine/tool defaults instead of registry lookups
forge_triple.mcp_action: prism_cam post_process_with_catalog — post-process with full catalog resolution
forge_triple.skill: /pp-resolve — resolve machine+material+tool from catalogs and show resolved context

units.title: Wire MachineRegistry into _resolveContexts() — replace hardcoded machine defaults
steps: Read _resolveContexts() in PostProcessorPipelineEngine.ts (lines 2579-2670) to understand current machine resolution
Import MachineRegistry (lazy load via _getEngine pattern or direct import)
In _resolveContexts(), when input.machine is a string (name only), call MachineRegistry.resolve(name) to get full MachineContext
Map registry fields: max_rpm, max_power_kW, max_torque_Nm, rapid_rate_mm_min, work_volume, axes, controller type, coolant_types, tsc_pressure_bar, tool_changer_time_s
Remove hardcoded fallbacks: max_rpm=12000, max_power_kW=15, rapid=30000 — replace with registry values or conservative defaults from registry median
Add resolution_confidence field: 1.0 if registry match found, 0.3 if fallback used
Add warning to pipeline result if machine not found in registry
exit_conditions: npx tsc --noEmit passes with 0 errors
Existing 117 PP tests still pass
New test: process({machine: 'Haas VF-2'}) resolves to max_rpm=8100, controller=haas
New test: process({machine: 'Unknown XYZ'}) falls back gracefully with resolution_confidence=0.3
A machinist would see correct machine limits in the output analytics

units.title: Wire MaterialRegistry into _resolveContexts() — replace regex ISO group inference
steps: Read _inferISOGroup() in PostProcessorPipelineEngine.ts to understand current regex-based inference
Import MaterialRegistry (lazy load)
In _resolveContexts(), when input.material is a string or has no kc1_1, call MaterialRegistry.resolve(name) to get full MaterialContext
Map registry fields: iso_group, kc1_1, mc, uts_MPa, hardness_HB, thermal_conductivity, specific_heat, jc_A/B/n/C/m (Johnson-Cook params)
Keep _inferISOGroup() as FINAL fallback only when registry has no match
Remove hardcoded material defaults — all physics-critical values come from registry or canonical constants
Add resolution_confidence: 1.0 for registry match, 0.5 for partial match, 0.2 for regex inference

Remove hardcoded defaults: type=flat_endmill, flute_count=4, material=carbide
Fall back to ToolGeometryDefaults.ts when registry has no match (diameter-based inference)
Add resolution_confidence per tool

Add SFO to _getEngine() lazy loader

Map SFO output (which includes CI, multiple resolvers, tribal knowledge) to existing stage output format
SFO internally calls MachineRegistry + MaterialRegistry + ToolRegistry — so U01-U03 wiring feeds through automatically
Keep UltimateSpeedFeedEngine as fallback if SFO fails
Propagate SFO confidence intervals through to Stage 4 (stochastic verification)

If physics S/F exceeds proven data by >20%: add warning 'physics exceeds shop-proven limits'

units.title: Wire CoolantRegistry + CoatingRegistry for Kienzle correction factors
steps: Import CoolantRegistry and CoatingRegistry (lazy load)
In Stage 1.1, after base kc1_1 is resolved, apply correction factors:
K_coolant: from CoolantRegistry — flood=1.0, MQL=0.95, dry=1.1, cryo=0.9
K_coating: from CoatingRegistry — TiAlN=0.85, TiN=0.9, AlCrN=0.82, uncoated=1.0
K_gamma: rake angle correction from tool geometry (gamma_ref=6°, K = 1 - 0.01*(gamma - gamma_ref))
K_wear: VB correction — K = 1 + 0.5*(VB/VB_max) (from wear tracking state)
Apply corrected kc = kc1_1 * K_coolant * K_coating * K_gamma * K_wear
Document correction factors in stage output for auditability
exit_conditions: npx tsc --noEmit passes
117 PP tests still pass
New test: flood coolant + TiAlN coating gives kc = kc1_1 * 1.0 * 0.85 = 15% reduction
New test: dry + uncoated gives kc = kc1_1 * 1.1 * 1.0 = 10% increase
Correction factors appear in analytics report

exit_gate: All 3 registries wired + SFO routing + proven data + correction factors. Pipeline uses real catalog data instead of hardcoded defaults. 117+ tests pass. /prism-review passed.
